stimulus: Despite the best efforts of journalists to be objective, it is inevitable that their own biases will enter their reporting, even if inadvertently. Therefore, it is imperative that a trained editor look over journalists’ work with an eye toward detecting and removing their biases, so as to make reporting as objective as possible.
questionStem: Each of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends except :

answerChoices.A: Journalists do not eliminate all of the biases that enter their reporting.
answerChoices.B: It is imperative that reporting be as objective as possible.
answerChoices.C: Objectivity in reporting is undermined by the presence of journalists’ biases.
answerChoices.D: Trained editors are able to detect at least some biases of journalists.
answerChoices.E: Journalists’ reporting that is not objective is not taken seriously by trained editors.

stimulus:
Astronomer: Mount Shalko is the perfect site for the proposed astronomical observatory. The summit would accommodate the complex as currently designed, with some room left for expansion. There are no large cities near the mountain, so neither smog nor artificial light interferes with atmospheric transparency. Critics claim that Mount Shalko is a unique ecological site, but the observatory need not be a threat to endemic life-forms. In fact, since it would preclude recreational use of the mountain, it should be
their salvation. It is estimated that 200,000 recreational users visit the mountain every year, posing a threat to the wildlife.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the astronomer’s argument?

answerChoices.A: More than a dozen insect and plant species endemic to Mount Shalko are found nowhere else on earth.
answerChoices.B: A coalition of 14 different groups, as diverse as taxpayer organizations and hunting associations, opposes the building of the new observatory.
answerChoices.C: Having a complex that covers most of the summit, as well as having the necessary security fences and access road on the mountain, could involve just as much ecological disruption as does the current level of recreational use.
answerChoices.D: The building of the observatory would not cause the small towns near Mount Shalko eventually to develop into a large city, complete with smog, bright lights, and an influx of recreation seekers.
answerChoices.E: A survey conducted by a team of park rangers concluded that two other mountains in the same general area have more potential for recreational use than Mount Shalko.

stimulus: The local fair held its annual photography contest and accepted entries from both amateur and professional photographers. However, when the awards were announced, the winners in each category were professionals. While this may seem to be an unusual result, it should not be surprising.
questionStem: Each of the following, if true, could by itself constitute an explanation of the result of the contest EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: Many more of the entries in the contest were from amateurs than from professionals.
answerChoices.B: The contest is widely advertised every year and the prize money is substantial.
answerChoices.C: The professionals had access to better equipment than the amateurs.
answerChoices.D: The judges for the contest were all professionals.
answerChoices.E: The categories were defined in such a way that amateur entries could not easily compete with the professional entries.

stimulus: The average 40-year-old North American will have watched more than one million TV commercials in his or her lifetime. We may safely conclude, therefore, that the TV commercial has influenced North American habits of thought.
questionStem: The conclusion above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The habits of thought that people develop are largely determined by external influences.
answerChoices.B: Anything people are exposed to in great quantity will influence their habits of thought.
answerChoices.C: It is impossible to avoid or ignore television commercials.
answerChoices.D: Some people find television commercials more interesting to watch than the programs themselves.
answerChoices.E: Certain forms of communication to which people are subjected will affect their habits of thought.

stimulus: Researchers have developed a membrane that quickly removes the oxygen from a refrigerator, thereby killing bacteria and enabling food to be stored almost indefinitely. Since food need not be kept as cold to prevent spoilage, energy costs will be greatly reduced. Thus, over the long run, oxygen-removing refrigerators will prove far less expensive than current models.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it does not

answerChoices.A: address the expense of building or refitting a refrigerator with the new technology
answerChoices.B: address the possibility of consumer discomfort with the new refrigerators
answerChoices.C: explain the technology that enabled the oxygen-removing membrane to be developed
answerChoices.D: take into account the effectiveness of current refrigerator technology in preventing food spoilage
answerChoices.E: take into account the inconvenience caused by food spoilage in current refrigerators

stimulus: Shortly after the power plant opened and began discharging its wastewater into the river, there was a notable increase in the algae population downstream from the discharge point. The algae in this river are known to feed on phosphorus and nitrogen compounds. The plant’s wastewater is free of such nutrients, but it does raise the temperature of the river water.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the increase in the algae population?

answerChoices.A: The wastewater contains trace amounts of detergents that are known to inhibit the growth of algae.
answerChoices.B: The algae population decreased in a nearby river that does not receive wastewater discharges.
answerChoices.C: Higher water temperatures increase the rate at which algae absorb nutrients already present in the river.
answerChoices.D: The plant’s wastewater contains dissolved oxygen, which is essential to the survival of fish but not to the survival of algae.
answerChoices.E: The river water’s temperature returns to normal within 2 miles of the discharge point.

stimulus: The existing works of ancient literature, science, and philosophy do not represent the most original work produced in ancient times. The most compelling evidence for this view is that the existing works frequently refer to other works that we no longer have.
questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if added to the argument, most helps to justify its conclusion?

answerChoices.A: Works that contain frequent references to other works tend to be derivative.
answerChoices.B: Many extant works have laudable things to say about the missing works.
answerChoices.C: A surprisingly large number of ancient texts have been irretrievably lost.
answerChoices.D: Subversive ideas tend to be suppressed whenever they are proposed.
answerChoices.E: Most current ideas regarded as original were already proposed in ancient times.

stimulus: A metaphor is the application of a word or phrase to something to which it does not literally apply in order to emphasize or indicate a similarity between that to which it would ordinarily apply and that to which it is—nonliterally—being applied. Some extremists claim that all uses of language are metaphorical. But this cannot be so, for unless some uses of words are literal, there can be no nonliteral uses of any words.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is not the case that all uses of language are metaphorical.
answerChoices.B: Either all uses of words are literal or all uses of words are metaphorical.
answerChoices.C: Nonliteral meaning is possible only if some uses of words employ their literal meanings.
answerChoices.D: Metaphors are nonliteral uses of language that can be used to suggest similarities between objects.
answerChoices.E: The ordinary meanings of words must be fixed by convention if the similarities between objects are to be representable by language.

stimulus: In a recent poll of chief executive officers (CEOs) of 125 large corporations, the overwhelming majority claimed that employee training and welfare is of the same high priority as customer satisfaction. So the popular belief that the top management of large corporations behaves indifferently to the needs and aspirations of employees is unfounded.
questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: fails to define adequately the term “top management”
answerChoices.B: presumes, without giving justification, that one is not indifferent to something that one considers a top priority
answerChoices.C: presumes, without giving justification, that the CEOs’ priorities tend to be misplaced
answerChoices.D: presumes, without giving justification, that the CEOs’ claims are reflected in actual practice
answerChoices.E: makes a generalization based on an unrepresentative sample

stimulus: Magazine editor: In recent years, subscriptions to our magazine have declined, but newsstand sales have increased. Since subscribers receive issues at a lower cost per issue than do newsstand purchasers, the magazine would increase revenue by eliminating discounted subscriptions altogether.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the editor’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: The magazine’s production costs will not increase in the near future.
answerChoices.B: Most newsstand purchasers would be unwilling to pay the current subscription price for the magazine.
answerChoices.C: Eliminating discounted subscriptions would not decrease newsstand sales.
answerChoices.D: The magazine’s content will remain the same after eliminating discounted subscriptions.
answerChoices.E: The total number of readers of the magazine would not decrease if discounted subscriptions were eliminated.

stimulus: The everyday behavior of whales is particularly difficult to study because introducing novel stimuli, such as divers or submarines, into the whales’ environment causes whales to behave in unusual ways. Some biologists plan to train sea lions to carry video cameras on their backs and, on command, to swim along with whales. They argue that since whales are accustomed to there being sea lions nearby, using the sea lions to film the whales would allow biologists to study the everyday behavior of the whales.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the biologists’ reasoning depends?

answerChoices.A: Whales will often react aggressively in the presence of divers and submarines although aggressive behavior is unusual for whales.
answerChoices.B: The behavior of the sea lions under human command will be within the range of sea lion behavior to which the whales are accustomed.
answerChoices.C: The trained sea lions will not be aware that they are carrying video cameras on their backs.
answerChoices.D: Sea lions carrying video cameras will be able to film whales at a much closer range than divers can.
answerChoices.E: Whales prefer the presence of sea lions to that of either divers or submarines.

stimulus: Historian: A city ordinance in the 1800s required chimneys to be cleaned monthly in order to prevent fires. Records show that fires decreased after the ordinance was enacted. Therefore, the monthly cleaning requirement reduced the number of fires.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to justify the historian’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: The ordinance was widely publicized in the city’s newspapers.
answerChoices.B: The city also enacted an ordinance that required fire extinguishers to be kept in all businesses.
answerChoices.C: People who failed to comply with the ordinance were subject to heavy fines.
answerChoices.D: The city hired additional fire inspectors during the 1800s.
answerChoices.E: The city’s population decreased during the period in which the ordinance was in effect.

stimulus:
Mall manager: By congregating in large groups near the stores in our mall, teenagers create an atmosphere in which many adult shoppers feel uncomfortable. As a result, the adults have begun to spend less time shopping than they have in the past. The mall’s goal in this situation is to prevent a significant loss in overall sales, so merchants should do their utmost to discourage teenagers from congregating near stores.

Merchant: But the amount spent by teenagers who congregate near mall stores constitutes a significant percentage of the total amount spent in those stores.
questionStem: The merchant’s response to the manager’s argument is most accurately described as

answerChoices.A: disputing the truth of claims the manager offers as support for the recommendation
answerChoices.B: giving information that pertains to the relation between the manager’s recommendation and the mall’s goal
answerChoices.C: suggesting that the mall’s goal is an undesirable one
answerChoices.D: contending that the manager’s recommendation is sound but for reasons other than those given by the manager
answerChoices.E: using the information cited by the manager to make an additional recommendation that would help achieve the goal

stimulus: Some dietary supplements are marketed as “natural,” implying that they are safer than synthetic supplements. However, many natural substances are toxic, and many synthetics are safe. Therefore, consumers should not assume that “natural” supplements are safer than synthetic ones.
questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Consumers are often misled by marketing terms.
answerChoices.B: The safety of a supplement depends on its chemical properties rather than its origin.
answerChoices.C: Natural supplements are less effective than synthetic supplements.
answerChoices.D: Synthetic supplements are regulated more strictly than natural supplements.
answerChoices.E: Consumers generally prefer natural supplements to synthetic ones.

stimulus: A survey of historians shows that most believe written texts to be the best source for historical understanding. None of the historians regarded painting, architecture, music, dance, or culinary arts as the best source for historical understanding. So these historians neglect many important repositories of historical knowledge.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument takes for granted that

answerChoices.A: there are no potential sources for historical understanding other than written texts and the arts
answerChoices.B: painting, architecture, music, dance, and culinary arts are important only as sources for historical understanding
answerChoices.C: there are no sources for historical understanding that are neither considered best by historians nor neglected by them
answerChoices.D: something other than written texts is the best source for historical understanding
answerChoices.E: the other sources for historical understanding mentioned by the historians surveyed are not important repositories of historical knowledge

stimulus: To act responsibly in one’s role as a citizen, one must be guided by a true understanding of the facts that bear on public decisions. Our newspaper therefore has an obligation to ensure that our readers are fully informed about the issues we cover.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: The newspaper’s readers are not fully informed about the issues it covers.
answerChoices.B: The newspaper is the best source of information on public issues.
answerChoices.C: The newspaper has an obligation to ensure that its readers are fully informed about the issues it covers.
answerChoices.D: A responsible citizen must be guided by a true understanding of the facts bearing on public decisions.
answerChoices.E: The newspaper should only cover issues that concern public decision-making.

stimulus: Linguist: The language of the Zed people has a complex system of verb endings that indicate not only tense but also the speaker’s degree of certainty. However, when Zed speakers use Zed words within sentences in another language, they often omit those endings. Therefore, in the Zed language, verb endings are not necessary for conveying meaning.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the linguist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: When Zed speakers use Zed words in other languages, they are often trying to make jokes or puns that depend on the absence of verb endings.
answerChoices.B: In Zed, the verb endings are required by the rules of grammar when speaking formally.
answerChoices.C: Zed speakers who are not fluent in other languages tend to include Zed verb endings even when speaking those languages.
answerChoices.D: Some Zed speakers use the endings inconsistently even when speaking Zed.
answerChoices.E: In the Zed language, the verb endings affect only the form of the verb and not the meaning.

stimulus: Chelas and Stelma are required to leave their respective stations immediately to pursue any prisoner who attempts to escape from their sector. Furthermore, unless they are pursuing such a prisoner, Chelas and Stelma are forbidden to leave their stations until their replacements have arrived. On May 11 at 9 P.M., when Chelas and Stelma finished the four-hour shift in their sector and their replacements arrived, it was discovered that Chelas had violated these rules and Stelma had not.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, each of the following could be true EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: Chelas and Stelma were at their respective stations at 9 P.M.
answerChoices.B: Stelma left her station before 9 P.M. but Chelas did not.
answerChoices.C: Chelas left his station before 9 P.M. but Stelma did not.
answerChoices.D: A prisoner attempted to escape from Chelas and Stelma’s sector at 7 P.M. and neither Chelas nor Stelma left his or her station before 9 P.M.
answerChoices.E: A prisoner attempted to escape from Chelas and Stelma’s sector at 7 P.M. and both Chelas and Stelma left their stations before 9 P.M.

stimulus:
Faden: Most of our exercise machines are still in use after one year. A recent survey of our customers shows this.

Greenwall: But many of those customers could easily be lying because they are too embarrassed to admit that they don’t exercise anymore.

Faden: You have no way of showing that customers were lying. Your objection is absurd.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Greenwall takes for granted that many customers have stopped using the equipment but are too embarrassed to admit it.
answerChoices.B: Greenwall presumes, without giving justification, that most people are dishonest about their personal habits.
answerChoices.C: Faden presumes, without providing justification, that the more conclusive the evidence is for a claim, the less believable the claim becomes.
answerChoices.D: Faden presumes, without providing justification, that the evidence for a claim has not been undermined unless that evidence has been proven false.
answerChoices.E: Greenwall ignores the possibility that some people stopped using the equipment but were not embarrassed about it

stimulus:
Sarah: Reporters, by allotting time to some events rather than others, are exercising their judgment as to what is newsworthy and what is not. In other words, they always interpret the news.

Ramon: Reporters should never interpret the news. Once they deem a story to be newsworthy, they are obliged to relay the facts to me untainted.
questionStem: Sarah and Ramon’s remarks provide the most support for holding that they disagree about the truth of which one of the following statements?

answerChoices.A: Reporters actually do interpret the news every time they report it.
answerChoices.B: Reporters should exercise their own judgment as to which events are newsworthy.
answerChoices.C: Reporters’ primary responsibility is to see that people are kept informed of the facts.
answerChoices.D: Reporters should not allot time to reporting some events rather than others.
answerChoices.E: Reporting on certain events rather than others qualifies as interpreting the news.

stimulus: Advertisement for a lactase supplement: Lactase, an enzyme produced by the body, aids in the digestion of lactose, a natural sugar found in dairy foods. Many subjects in an experiment who drank a liter of milk on an empty stomach showed signs of lactose intolerance—difficulty in digesting dairy products because of insufficient lactase. Thus, extrapolating from the number of subjects adversely affected, at least 50 million people in North America alone should take lactase supplements.
questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Eating solid food when drinking milk can decrease the amount of lactase produced by the body.
answerChoices.B: Most people who consume dairy products consume less lactose at each meal than the amount found in a liter of milk.
answerChoices.C: The production of lactase by the human body increases with age.
answerChoices.D: Lactose intolerance can interfere with proper nutrition.
answerChoices.E: Some dairy foods, such as cheese, contain a form of lactose more difficult to digest than that found in milk.

stimulus:
Jim: I hear that the company is considering giving Fred and Dorothy 25 percent raises. That would make their salaries higher than mine. Since I have worked here longer than they have, it would be unfair to raise their salaries unless mine is raised to at least what theirs will be.

Tasha: Thirty-five employees have been here the same length of time you have and earn the same salary you earn. It would be unfair to raise your salary without raising theirs.
questionStem: Which one of the following principles most helps to justify both parties’ statements?

answerChoices.A: In order to be fair, a business must pay identical salaries to employees with identical duties.
answerChoices.B: In order to be fair, a business must pay an employee a salary commensurate with his or her experience in the field.
answerChoices.C: In order to be fair, a business must always pay one employee more than another if the first employee has worked for the company longer than the second has.
answerChoices.D: In order to be fair, a business must never pay one employee more than another unless the first employee has worked for the company longer than the second has.
answerChoices.E: In order to be fair, a business must always pay employees a salary commensurate with the amount of time they work every day.

stimulus: Commentator: A political constitution that provides the framework for the laws of a nation must be interpreted to apply to new situations not envisioned by its authors. Although these interpretations express the moral and political beliefs of the interpreters, they are usually portrayed as embodying the intentions of the authors. This fiction is vital because without it the illusion, so necessary for political stability, that laws are the bequest of a long tradition rather than the preferences of contemporary politicians would vanish.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the commentator’s statements, if they are true?

answerChoices.A: If the people of a nation do not believe that the laws under which they live express the intentions of their political leaders, that nation will become more politically unstable.
answerChoices.B: Political instability will increase if the people of a nation cease to believe that their constitution is being interpreted consistently with the intentions of its authors.
answerChoices.C: Political instability will ensue if people come to believe there is a divergence between the beliefs of the authors of their constitution and those of their present political leaders.
answerChoices.D: A written constitution preserves the illusion that laws are the bequest of a long tradition rather than the creations of modern politicians.
answerChoices.E: The perceived lack of a long legal tradition in a nation makes the political stability of that nation dependent upon the fiction that its present political leaders share the intentions of the authors of the constitution of that nation.

stimulus: Only if a family manages its finances wisely will it obtain fiscal security. But without realistic projections of financial obligations, a functional budget cannot be devised. So, if either fiscal security is to be obtained or a workable budget devised, finances must be managed wisely or financial obligations must be projected realistically.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its pattern of reasoning to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Without continued use of pesticides it is not possible to grow enough food for the world’s people. But only when researchers develop pesticides harmless to humans will persistent health problems be reduced. Thus, pesticide use must continue or pesticides harmless to humans must be developed if enough food is to be produced or persistent health problems are to be reduced.
answerChoices.B: Reasonably healthy people who wish to lose weight must alter their balance of caloric intake and caloric burn off. But without benefit of medical supervision, drastic changes in diet or exercise patterns would be harmful. So, one who wishes to lose weight but does not want to risk health problems should seek medical supervision before beginning a diet or exercise program.
answerChoices.C: Many popular, low-maintenance houseplants are available. Yet some of these plants, because they are toxic, are unsuitable for homes where pets are kept indoors. As a result, pet owners should either select nontoxic plants or keep the plants out of a pet’s reach if they want low-maintenance houseplants or cannot keep their pets outside.
answerChoices.D: Only employees who work diligently will be retained in this company until they are eligible for retirement. Also, we can retain only those employees who fit the new organizational structure of our proposed redesign process. So, if this redesign process is carried out, any employee who seeks continuing employment here must work diligently and fit the new organizational structure.
answerChoices.E: A successful charity drive requires detailed planning. Volunteers must be recruited and trained, and equipment and facilities must be prepared months before the drive is to begin. Thus, if a group is organizing a charity drive, the group must formulate a detailed plan well ahead of time or it can expect failure.

stimulus: Anthropologist: A study of vervet monkeys found that they respond to certain calls by looking to specific group members. This could be explained if the monkeys know the dominance hierarchy among members of their troupe. Primatologist: That is unwarranted. You can predict the output of a bank cash machine by knowing customers’ requests, but this does not show that the machine itself knows anything. Similarly, predictions based on the monkeys’ responses do not show that the monkeys know the dominance hierarchy.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the point at issue between the anthropologist and the primatologist?

answerChoices.A: whether vervet monkeys know the dominance hierarchy of their troupe
answerChoices.B: whether vervet monkeys can use knowledge of dominance hierarchies to make predictions
answerChoices.C: whether anthropologists should apply analogies from machines to animals
answerChoices.D: whether vervet monkeys’ behavior can be predicted on the basis of their responses
answerChoices.E: whether vervet monkeys’ calls can be distinguished by other species

stimulus:
Anthropologist: After mapping the complete dominance hierarchy for a troupe of vervet monkeys by examining their pairwise interaction, we successfully predicted more complex forms of their group behavior by assuming that each monkey had knowledge of the complete hierarchy. Since our prediction was so accurate, it follows that the assumption we used to reach it was in fact true.

Primatologist: Although I agree that your assumption helped you make those predictions, your conclusion does not follow. You might as well argue that since we can predict the output of some bank cash machines by assuming that these machines actually want to satisfy the customers’ requests, these cash machines must really have desires.
questionStem: Which one of the following is a point about which the anthropologist and the primatologist are committed to disagreeing?

answerChoices.A: whether the anthropologist successfully predicted the behavior of individual monkeys by use of the map of the troupe’s dominance hierarchy
answerChoices.B: whether the output of a bank cash machine can be accurately predicted on the basis of knowledge of the requests made to it by customers
answerChoices.C: whether vervet monkeys can have knowledge of the complete hierarchy of dominance relations that exists within their own troupe
answerChoices.D: whether the fact that the anthropologist’s assumption led to such successful predictions provides sufficient grounds for the claim that the vervet monkeys had knowledge of their dominance hierarchy
answerChoices.E: whether the behavior exhibited by vervet monkeys in experimental situations can be used as the basis for a generalization concerning all vervet monkeys
